extracted.intended_audience: water system operators, state primacy agencies, certified laboratories, public health stakeholders, and other regulated parties involved in drinking water regulation
extracted.subtask_description: Excerpts from the EPA proposed National Primary Drinking Water Regulation (NPDWR) for perchlorate, including preamble discussion and the proposed regulatory text specifying monitoring, analytical, compliance, implementation, and administrative requirements for public water systems and laboratories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy effects analysis / consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA evaluated whether the proposed rule would adversely affect the supply, distribution, or use of energy and concluded it "is not likely to have a significant adverse effect on the supply, distribution, or use of energy."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA assessed number of systems expected to require incremental power at various proposed MCLs (e.g., ~100 systems at 20 µg/L; ~60 at 40 µg/L; ~20 at 80 µg/L) and determined increased peak electricity demand at water utilities is negligible; therefore existing electrical connections are adequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of voluntary consensus standards (NTTAA)
rubrics_metrics.description: This action involves technical standards. The EPA proposes to use voluntary consensus standards that would require monitoring for perchlorate and analysis of the samples obtained from monitoring based on required methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA proposed five analytical methods for identification and quantification of perchlorate in drinking water (EPA Methods 314.0, 314.1, 314.2, 331.0, and 332.0) which incorporate quality control criteria allowing accurate quantitation; documents made available via regulations.gov and EPA Drinking Water Docket. EPA welcomes comments and identification of potentially applicable voluntary consensus standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public invitation to identify voluntary consensus standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA welcomes comments on this aspect of the proposed rulemaking and, specifically, invites the public to identify potentially applicable voluntary consensus standards and to explain why such standards should be used in this regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director of the Federal Register approved the voluntary consensus standards incorporated by reference in 40 CFR 141.23 as of April 11, 2007; EPA will continue to make related documents available through docket sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation with advisory bodies and interagency review
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA consulted with the National Drinking Water Advisory Council (NDWAC), the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS), and the EPA Science Advisory Board (SAB) in accordance with SDWA sections 1412(d) and 1412(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA considered NDWAC recommendations (e.g., January 10, 2025 meeting summary) and SAB input (e.g., May 29, 2013 SAB Advice) during development of the proposed perchlorate NPDWR; EPA also initiated consultation with HHS and considered HHS input as part of interagency review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of PBPK/BBDR models and life-stage approach for MCLG derivation
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA collaborated with FDA scientists to develop PBPK/pharmacodynamic (PD), or biologically based dose-response (BBDR), models that incorporate available health information on perchlorate to estimate changes in thyroid hormones in sensitive life stages and derived a Maximum Contaminant Level Goal (MCLG) informed by those models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models were developed based on perchlorate's mode of action (iodide uptake inhibition by the thyroid) per SAB recommendations; EPA developed a two-step approach to integrate BBDR model results with epidemiological neurodevelopmental outcome data to link maternal thyroid hormone changes to neurodevelopment and derive an MCLG addressing the most sensitive life stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial monitoring: groundwater systems >10,000 persons & surface water systems (no acceptable historic data)
rubrics_metrics.description: All ground water systems serving greater than 10,000 persons without acceptable historic data and all surface water systems without acceptable historic data must collect four initial consecutive quarterly samples at all sampling points by [INSERT DATE 3 YEARS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement appears in proposed §141.23(c)(10)(i); acceptable historic data as defined in paragraph (c)(10)(v) may substitute (see separate criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial monitoring: ground water systems ≤10,000 persons (no acceptable historic data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ground water systems serving 10,000 persons or fewer without acceptable historic data must collect two initial samples between five and seven months apart at all sampling points by [INSERT DATE 3 YEARS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified in proposed §141.23(c)(10)(ii); data timing and sample-count parity requirements apply for accepting historical data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent monitoring frequencies based on initial monitoring results
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on initial monitoring results, systems must monitor at specified frequencies beginning [INSERT DATE 3 YEARS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER]: (A) Any system with all initial samples at or below 4.0 µg/L at a sampling point shall take one sample at that sampling point during each compliance cycle (i.e., nine years). (B) Surface water systems with all initial samples at or below the MCL and any above 4.0 µg/L at a sampling point shall take one sample annually at the sampling point. (C) Ground water systems with all initial samples at or below the MCL and any above 4.0 µg/L at a sampling point shall take one sample at that sampling point during each compliance period (i.e., three years). (D) Any system with an initial monitoring result above the MCL shall monitor quarterly at that sampling point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These monitoring frequencies are in §141.23(c)(10)(iii) and delineate reduced-frequency options tied to initial concentration tiers (≤4.0 µg/L, ≤MCL but >4.0 µg/L, >MCL).

rubrics_metrics.name: State authority to increase sampling frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: States may increase the frequency of sampling in paragraph (c)(10)(iii) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits primacy agencies to require more frequent monitoring than federal baseline frequencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of historical data to satisfy initial monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: States may accept historical data by a water system to satisfy the initial monitoring requirements if systems use monitoring data for a sampling point using the same number of samples specified in paragraphs (c)(10)(i) and (ii), or data that was collected under a state monitoring requirement, collected between January 1, 2021 and [INSERT DATE OF PUBLICATION OF THE FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER] to satisfy the initial monitoring requirements for that sampling point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides flexibility to substitute comparable prior monitoring datasets provided they meet sample-count and time-window criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmation sampling following an exceedance
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the results of sampling for perchlorate indicate an exceedance of the maximum contaminant level, the systems must take a confirmation sample within five days of the system's receipt of notification of the analytical results of the first sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified in §141.23(f)(3); timeliness (within five days) is enforced for confirmation of initial exceedances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Averaging initial and confirmation samples when state-required confirmation is taken
rubrics_metrics.description: If a State-required confirmation sample is taken for any contaminant, then the results of the initial and confirmation sample shall be averaged. The resulting average shall be used to determine the system's compliance in accordance with paragraph (i) of this section. States have the discretion to delete results of obvious sampling errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified in §141.23(f)(4); allows states to remove obvious sampling error results at their discretion before averaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance determination rule for nitrate, nitrite, and perchlorate
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with the maximum contaminant levels for nitrate, nitrite, and perchlorate is determined based on one sample if the levels of these contaminants are below the MCLs. If the level of perchlorate exceeds the MCL in the initial sample, a confirmation sample is required in accordance with paragraph (f)(3) of this section, and compliance shall be based on the average of the initial and confirmation sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirrors approach for nitrate/nitrite; initial single-sample compliance when below MCL, otherwise average of initial+confirmation governs compliance determination (see §141.23(i)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required analytical methods and alternatives / equivalency
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis for the following contaminants shall be conducted in accordance with the methods in the following table, or the alternative methods listed in appendix A to subpart C of this part, or their equivalent as determined by EPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria for analyzing various inorganic contaminants and test procedures are contained in Technical Notes on Drinking Water Methods, EPA-600/R-94-173; EPA can determine equivalence of alternative methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference of approved compliance methods for perchlorate
rubrics_metrics.description: The approved compliance methods for determining perchlorate in drinking water listed in table 1 to paragraph (k) of this section, are incorporated by reference. The Director of the Federal Register approves this incorporation by reference in accordance with 5 U.S.C. 552(a) and 1 CFR part 51.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of material incorporated by reference may be inspected at EPA's Drinking Water Docket or at NARA; establishes enforceable reliance on specified approved methods (e.g., EPA Methods 314.*, 331.0, 332.0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample collection, preservation, container, and holding time procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample collection for antimony, arsenic, asbestos, barium, beryllium, cadmium, chromium, cyanide, fluoride, mercury, nickel, nitrate, nitrite, perchlorate, selenium, and thallium under this section shall be conducted using the sample preservation, container, and maximum holding time procedures specified in the table below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laboratories and systems must follow the specified sample handling procedures in the referenced table to ensure valid analytical results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory certification requirement for analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis under this section shall only be conducted by laboratories that have been certified by EPA or the State. Laboratories may conduct sample analysis under provisional certification until January 1, 1996. To receive certification to conduct analyses for ... perchlorate ... the laboratory must: * * *
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that only EPA- or state-certified labs may perform compliance analyses for perchlorate and lists (elsewhere in the rule) the requirements labs must meet to obtain certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates for compliance and specific provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations contained in the revisions to §§ 141.23(...), 141.51(b), 141.60(b)(5), 141.62(...), appendices, etc., are effective for the purposes of compliance on [INSERT DATE 3 YEARS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE FEDERAL REGISTER]. The effective date for §141.62(b)(17) is [DATE OF PUBLICATION OF FINAL RULE IN THE Federal Register].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule sets staggered effective dates: a general 3-year compliance start for many provisions and a publication-date effective date for at least one MCL entry; systems and states must track these differing dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition of Perchlorate to MCLG and regulated contaminants lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend §141.51 by revising table 1 to paragraph (b) by adding in alphabetical order, an entry for 'Perchlorate'. Amend appendix A to subpart O of part 141 under the heading 'Inorganic contaminants' by adding an entry for 'Perchlorate' in alphabetical order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal inclusion of perchlorate in the lists of regulated contaminants and corresponding MCLG/MCL entries; affects monitoring and compliance obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of affordable technologies / BATs for small systems (≤10,000 persons)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator, pursuant to section 1412 of the Act, hereby identifies in the following table the affordable technology, treatment technique, or other means available to systems serving 10,000 persons or fewer for achieving compliance with the maximum contaminant level for perchlorate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key to BATs lists specific technologies (e.g., 5 = Ion Exchange; 7 = Reverse Osmosis; 14 = Biological Treatment in §141.62; Part 142 uses 13 = Biological Treatment). EPA also issues documents describing Best Available Technologies and Small System Compliance Technologies and Technologies and Costs for treating perchlorate-contaminated waters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notification and standard health effects language for perchlorate violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend appendix A to subpart Q (NPDWR Violations and Other Situations Requiring Public Notice) and appendix B to subpart Q (Standard Health Effects Language for Public Notification) by adding entries for 'Perchlorate' in alphabetical order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix A endnote: Primacy agencies may at their option require a more stringent public notice tier; appendix B endnotes define MCLG and MCL; inclusion means specific notice tiers and standardized health-effect language will apply to perchlorate violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of perchlorate in variances and exemptions implementation (Part 142)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend table 1 to paragraph (b) in §142.62 by adding an entry for 'Perchlorate' in alphabetical order, and an entry '13 = Biological Treatment' under the undesignated heading entitled 'Key to BATs'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part 142 implements variances and exemptions and links allowable technologies (BATs) for small systems; adding perchlorate enables the variance/exemption framework to apply to perchlorate MCL compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability threshold for 'public water system' (SDWA definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: SDWA section 1401(4), 42 U.S.C. 300f(4), defines 'public water system' as 'a system for the provision to the public of water for human consumption through pipes or other constructed conveyances, if such system has at least fifteen service connections or regularly serves at least twenty-five individuals.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the population/connection thresholds that determine which systems are subject to the monitoring, treatment, and public-notification requirements of the regulation.
